text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.2% today, capping a sharp 1.5% decline over two weeks. The stock has been hammered since mid-November, dropping roughly $47 per share from $414 to $367. The trigger appears to be a combination of factors: oil prices have softened (US crude around $89.50, down from levels that would have supported higher refining margins), and the geopolitical uncertainty in the Strait of Hormuz noted on November 18th—a key shipping chokepoint for global energy—has weighed on energy sector confidence without pushing prices high enough to help refiners' profit margins.

Refinery utilization remains robust at 95.7%, so the problem isn't lack of work. Rather, refiners like Marathon profit most when the gap between crude input costs and product prices widens; softer oil prices and ample inventory levels (gasoline and diesel storage both elevated) suggest that margin compression has pressured the entire sector. The geopolitical stress in the Middle East, combined with European energy tightness, creates uncertainty rather than the sustained price rally that would typically benefit a large refiner.
